hotels.name: Edmonton Hotel & Convention Centre
hotels.notes: Placeholder while we finalize hotels. A few minutes from the Grand Imperial.

travel.intro: Most guests fly into Edmonton International (YEG). The venues are in south Edmonton, about 30 minutes from the airport.

airports.name: Edmonton International
airports.tips: Direct flights from major Canadian hubs. Connections from India typically through Toronto or Vancouver.

airports.name: Calgary International
airports.tips: Calgary works if that is where you land, but it is about a 3 hour drive and not a quick trip. Fly into YEG when you can.

gettingAround.title: Rideshare and taxis
gettingAround.text: Uber and taxis are available throughout the area.

gettingAround.title: Car rental
gettingAround.text: A rental car is recommended. The venues are a short drive apart in south Edmonton. Parking is free.

gettingAround.title: Transit
gettingAround.text: ETS buses and the LRT may not be a convenient way to the venues, so plan on a car or rideshare.

international.title: Travelling from outside Canada
international.text: Check entry requirements early. Visitors from visa-exempt countries need an eTA (about CAD $7, usually approved within minutes). Others may need a visitor visa, which can take weeks. We are happy to provide an invitation letter; message a coordinator.

aroundTown.name: Edmonton River Valley
aroundTown.text: North America's largest urban park, along the North Saskatchewan. In July the trails are easy walking and cycling, with picnic spots and views from the bridges.
aroundTown.address: North Saskatchewan River Valley, Edmonton, AB

aroundTown.name: Muttart Conservatory
aroundTown.text: Four glass pyramids of tropical, desert and temperate gardens in the river valley. A calm hour indoors if the afternoon is hot or rainy.

aroundTown.name: Fort Edmonton Park
aroundTown.text: Living history on 158 acres in the river valley, open through the summer. Period streets, rides and interpreters; give it a few hours.

aroundTown.name: Elk Island National Park
aroundTown.text: Bison, elk and prairie lakes about 45 minutes east of the city. A morning trip if you have a car.
aroundTown.address: 1-54401 Range Road 203, Fort Saskatchewan, AB T8L 0V3

aroundTown.name: Suvai Dosa's Pure Veg
aroundTown.text: South Indian cooking in Mill Woods, a short drive from the hotels, and the menu is entirely vegetarian. Order idli, medu vada and a crisp masala dosa.

aroundTown.name: All India Restaurant & Sweets
aroundTown.text: A Mill Woods kitchen since 2006, with sweets made in the shop every day. Vegetarian dishes are marked on the menu; take gulab jamun or jalebi back with you.

aroundTown.name: Khazana
aroundTown.text: The downtown dining room for a proper Indian meal. Edify named it Edmonton's best Indian restaurant in 2025; order the samosas, pakoras, dal and paneer.

aroundTown.name: Padmanadi
aroundTown.text: Indonesian cooking from a family kitchen open since 2002, and the entire menu is vegan. Try the tom yum, spicy eggplant, tofu curry or ginger soy beef. The 101 Street dining room is the one to book; a smaller spot on Gateway Boulevard is closer to the hotels.

aroundTown.name: An Chay
aroundTown.text: A small Vietnamese restaurant on Jasper Avenue, and every dish is vegetarian. Start with the tofu rolls or green papaya salad, then a bowl of satay or lemongrass noodle soup.
aroundTown.address: 11203 Jasper Ave NW, Edmonton, AB T5K 0L5

aroundTown.name: Café Mosaics
aroundTown.text: A Whyte Avenue spot for a casual vegetarian meal: vegan wings, loaded nachos and all-day breakfast. Easy to pair with an afternoon in Old Strathcona.

aroundTown.name: Old Strathcona Farmers' Market
aroundTown.text: Edmonton's original indoor market, just off Whyte Avenue. Open Saturday 8 to 3 and Sunday 11 to 3, with growers, baking and local makers.

aroundTown.name: Whyte Avenue
aroundTown.text: Old Strathcona's main street of independent shops, bookstores and patios. Easy to combine with the farmers' market or Café Mosaics.

aroundTown.name: West Edmonton Mall
aroundTown.text: One of the largest malls in the world: shopping, an indoor waterpark and an amusement park. A reliable afternoon if the weather turns.

For those who have asked, we've put together a small registry, and a contribution toward our first home together would be warmly appreciated.

faq.q: What are Mehendi, Haldi and Vidhi, and the wedding?
faq.a: Mehendi is an evening of henna. Haldi and Vidhi is a morning blessing where turmeric paste is applied to the couple. The wedding is our marriage ceremony, with vows around the sacred fire.

faq.q: What should I wear to each event?
faq.a: Mehendi: colourful and comfortable. Haldi and Vidhi: yellow or white. Turmeric stains, so wear something you don't mind ruining. Wedding: colourful and comfortable — wear whatever you feel comfortable in. Rich, elegant colours are welcome; it is better to avoid black.
The wedding menu is fully vegetarian.

faq.q: Do you have a registry? What about cash gifts?
faq.a:
Your presence at our wedding is the greatest gift of all.
We kindly request no presents or covers—only your blessings and warm wishes.
Parking is free at every venue. Accessible spaces are beside each main entrance.
Shuttles are not confirmed or coordinated yet. We will update this page when we have news. Until then, we recommend a rental car or rideshare.
Please arrive 15 to 20 minutes early so you can find your seat before each event begins.
